markets.macro_note: Rates softer, Fed signals no rate hike series coming, small caps bleeding out.

big_story.story_title: Levi Strauss hikes profit guidance after tariff refunds, but its sales outlook is less optimistic
big_story.angle: Levi's profit beat is entirely a tariff accounting gift, not operational strength—the company is guiding down on actual demand, which is the real story buried under the headline.

quick_hits.angle: Fed minutes show zero appetite for rate hikes despite inflation noise—this is the permission slip for equities to keep grinding higher.
Anthropic's IPO is being pre-hyped as 'most ridiculous' of the year by analysts who are basically admitting they have no idea how to value it.
Modelo owner Constellation is getting creative to bring back beer drinkers—when your fix is 'creativity' instead of product, demand is actually broken.
Teenage Engineering's CEO says it'll stop making synths—a boutique hardware maker admitting the economics don't work is a quiet signal that niche manufacturing is dead.

odd_thing.joke_angle: A supertanker just chartered for $76M to haul stuff from the Gulf to China—that's 10x pre-war rates, which means someone's betting the shipping market is now a geopolitical hostage situation.

yesterday_callback.topic: Meta Muse popularity lifts AMD stock to fresh highs as AI agents juice CPU sales
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: AMD is up 2.8% today on chip demand, but the real move is Cisco +4.54%—the networking gear play on AI infrastructure is outrunning the chip itself, suggesting the margin is in the plumbing, not the silicon.
